lines.raw: **Original Medicare** is the government-run path: **Part A** pays hospitals and **Part B** pays doctors and outpatient care, each with its own premium, deductible and cost sharing.

lines.raw: Part B pays for **doctor visits**, outpatient hospital care (like an emergency room visit without admission), **lab tests**, X-rays, ambulance rides, wheelchairs and other equipment, and some drugs given in a clinic, like injections.
lines.say: Part B pays for doctor visits, outpatient hospital care (like an emergency room visit without admission), lab tests, X-rays, ambulance rides, wheelchairs and other equipment, and some drugs given in a clinic, like injections.

lines.raw: Many **preventive services** are free, such as the yearly **wellness visit**, flu shots and some cancer screenings.
lines.say: Many preventive services are free, such as the yearly wellness visit, flu shots and some cancer screenings.

lines.raw: Everyone pays a monthly **premium**: the standard amount is **$185 per month in 2025**.
lines.say: Everyone pays a monthly premium: the standard amount is 185 dollars per month in 2025.

lines.raw: People with high incomes pay more.
lines.say: People with high incomes pay more.

lines.raw: Many people have it taken straight out of their Social Security payment.
lines.say: Many people have it taken straight out of their Social Security payment.

lines.raw: There is a yearly **deductible** of **$257 in 2025**.
lines.say: There is a yearly deductible of 257 dollars in 2025.

lines.raw: After that, the patient usually pays **20% coinsurance** of the Medicare-approved amount.
lines.say: After that, the patient usually pays 20 percent coinsurance of the Medicare-approved amount.

scenes.section: Worked example: a Part B bill

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: 1. Deductible. Calculation: First $257 of the approved amount. Robert pays: $257.00. Medicare pays: $0.00.
lines.say: 1. Deductible. Calculation: First 257 dollars of the approved amount. Robert pays: 257 dollars. Medicare pays: 0 dollars.

lines.raw: 2. Coinsurance. Calculation: 20% of the remaining $43 ($300 − $257). Robert pays: $8.60. Medicare pays: $34.40.
lines.say: 2. Coinsurance. Calculation: 20 percent of the remaining 43 dollars (300 dollars − 257 dollars). Robert pays: 8 dollars 60 cents. Medicare pays: 34 dollars 40 cents.

lines.raw: **Total**. Robert pays: **$265.60**. Medicare pays: **$34.40**.
lines.say: Total. Robert pays: 265 dollars 60 cents. Medicare pays: 34 dollars 40 cents.

lines.raw: Original Medicare Part B, first visit of the year.
lines.say: Original Medicare Part B, first visit of the year.

lines.raw: patient pays equals deductible plus 20% times (approved − deductible).
lines.say: patient pays equals deductible plus 20 percent times (approved − deductible).

lines.raw: For example: $257 plus 20% times $43 equals $257 plus $8.60 equals $265.60.
lines.say: For example: 257 dollars plus 20 percent times 43 dollars equals 257 dollars plus 8 dollars 60 cents equals 265 dollars 60 cents.

lines.raw: Medicare pays $300 − $265.60 equals $34.40.
lines.say: Medicare pays 300 dollars − 265 dollars 60 cents equals 34 dollars 40 cents.

lines.raw: Original Medicare data splits along the same line as the cover.
lines.say: Original Medicare data splits along the same line as the cover.

lines.raw: **Part A** hospital bills arrive as **institutional** claims and **Part B** doctor bills as **professional** claims, both processed by a MAC.
lines.say: Part A hospital bills arrive as institutional claims and Part B doctor bills as professional claims, both processed by a M A C.

lines.raw: The approved amount sits where commercial data has the allowed amount, and deductibles follow **benefit periods** for Part A but the **calendar year** for Part B, so do not assume one deductible per person per year.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: Original Medicare = Parts A and B, paid by the government through contractors called MACs.
lines.say: Original Medicare = Parts A and B, paid by the government through contractors called M A C's.

lines.raw: Part A pays the hospital; the doctors who treat you in hospital are paid by Part B.
lines.say: Part A pays the hospital; the doctors who treat you in hospital are paid by Part B.

lines.raw: The Part A deductible applies per benefit period, not per calendar year.
lines.say: The Part A deductible applies per benefit period, not per calendar year.

lines.raw: In 2025: Part A deductible $1,676 per benefit period; Part B premium $185 a month and deductible $257 a year, then usually 20%.
lines.say: In 2025: Part A deductible 1676 dollars per benefit period; Part B premium 185 dollars a month and deductible 257 dollars a year, then usually 20 percent.

lines.raw: Original Medicare has no yearly out-of-pocket maximum.
lines.say: Original Medicare has no yearly out-of-pocket maximum.
